s1.syndrome_frame: painful vulvar swelling with signs of inflammation
salient_findings: extremely painful during the past week
signs of inflammation on local examination
key_facts: left labial swelling with signs of inflammation
pain decreased and inflammation subsided after antibiotics
5 × 5 cm firm swelling of the left labia majora

raw.syndrome_frame: painful vulvar swelling with signs of inflammation
salient_findings: extremely painful during the past week
signs of inflammation on local examination
key_facts: left labial swelling with signs of inflammation
pain decreased and inflammation subsided after antibiotics
5 × 5 cm firm swelling of the left labia majora

shortlist.label: Bartholin's abscess
shortlist.why_kept: initial clinical diagnosis with signs of inflammation

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: firm, non-cystic mass with decreased pain after antibiotics

shortlist.label: Vulvar leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: firm swelling with no signs of inflammation or malignancy

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: firm, non-cystic mass with no signs of inflammation or malignancy

shortlist.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
shortlist.why_kept: rare, but possible cause of a firm, painless vulvar mass

raw.rationale: The firm, 5 × 5 cm swelling of the left labia majora without signs of inflammation, and the patient's response to initial antibiotic treatment not being indicative of an infectious process, points towards a benign tumor such as vulvar leiomyoma.

rejected.label: Bartholin's abscess
rejected.why: Initial diagnosis was reconsidered due to the swelling being firm and not cystic, and the lack of continued signs of infection after antibiotic treatment.

rejected.label: Epidermoid cyst
rejected.why: The swelling was described as firm, not cystic, which is less typical for an epidermoid cyst.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: While possible, the description does not specifically suggest a lipoma, and other options better fit the clinical presentation.

rejected.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
rejected.why: This condition is rare and typically presents with a larger, more infiltrative mass, which does not align perfectly with the described firm, localized swelling.
